chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The tooth, when it is struck, is awaited for a year; if it falls out, the striker is fined five hundred dirhams, and if it does not fall out but blackens, he is fined two-thirds of its wergild.

key_terms.أُغْرِمَ: He was fined / liable for payment

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on compensation for a broken or blackened tooth?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific financial compensation (diyah) for dental injury, establishing a one-year observation period to determine if the tooth is lost or merely discolored. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on precise quantification of bodily damages, distinguishing between total loss (fixed 500 dirhams) and partial damage (two-thirds of the tooth's value), thereby ensuring equitable restitution in legal disputes.
